quirks: Nueva Italia (also called Colonia Nueva Italia) is not a separate FamilySearch place — all civil and parish records are filed under Parácuaro municipality. Search Parácuaro for all records.

Civil nacimientos have documented gaps: years 1913, 1914, 1915, and 1918 produce no indexed volumes in FamilySearch volume_search, and the FamilySearch Catalog film note for this municipality explicitly lists only Nacimientos 1910-1912, 1916-1917, 1919-1922 on a single film (DGS 4871475). Those four years appear absent from the civil record; use Catholic bautismos as the parallel and substitute source.

Catholic bautismos for 1906–1921 are available and 96–97% name-indexed on FamilySearch (collection 1883388). These volumes cover the entire target period, including the gap years missing from civil registration.

The catalog creator for the Parácuaro parish registers is 'Archivo Diocesano de Apatzingán,' but a separate catalog note also references 'archivo diocesano de Zamora.' Both archives may hold copies; in 1905–1920 the Tierra Caliente was under the Diocese of Zamora before the Diocese of Apatzingán was created in 1961.

A second chapel — Santa Ana, El Caulote (formerly Furicato), with bautismos 1902–1918 indexed on FamilySearch — also serves part of Parácuaro municipality. If a family cannot be found in the main Parácuaro parish, search El Caulote as well.

No FamilySearch indexed collections were returned by collections_search for Michoacán in the 1905–1920 window, but the civil and parish volumes are fully available through volume_search (100 total volumes, all online) and the statewide FamilySearch collections 1916243 (civil) and 1883388 (Catholic church).

Civil registration in Mexico was established by law on 28 July 1859 at the municipio level and was vigorously enforced from 1867 onward, per https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Mexico_Civil_Registration. For births before that enforcement, only Catholic parish records exist.

The sibling evidence (Miguel, Liborio, Facundo Cruz born 1913–1918 in Guerrero) suggests the family may have been in neighboring Guerrero during the years missing from Parácuaro's civil register. Guerrero civil registration is also online at FamilySearch (collection 1918291, 1860-1996). Search both states.

Parácuaro is in the Tierra Caliente region of Michoacán. Adjoining municipalities include Apatzingán (northwest), Tepalcatepec (southwest), and La Huacana (east). If no record appears for Parácuaro, check neighboring municipios' records at FamilySearch.

All records are in Spanish. Older entries (pre-1900) are in narrative handwritten style; records in the 1905-1920 period use formatted ledger registers. The Spanish Genealogical Word List at https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Spanish_Genealogical_Word_List is the primary paleography aid.
entry.guide_markdown:
# Locality Guide: Nueva Italia (Parácuaro Municipality), Michoacán, Mexico (1905–1920)

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Formed:** Parácuaro municipality recognized 1861. Nueva Italia (Colonia Nueva Italia) is a community within this municipality and has no separate civil or ecclesiastical record-keeping jurisdiction.
- **Administrative center:** Parácuaro (the municipio seat), Michoacán
- **Parent jurisdiction:** State of Michoacán (became a Mexican state 22 December 1823); records at the municipio level
- **Population during period:** No population data was returned by FamilySearch tools for this municipio. Wikipedia identifies Nueva Italia as being in the Tierra Caliente (hot lowlands) region of Michoacán.
- **Economy:** Agriculture, including large hacienda / colonization enterprises (Nueva Italia was itself a colonization project in the Tierra Caliente).
- **Religious denominations:** Roman Catholic, the overwhelmingly dominant denomination. The Parácuaro parish church is Nuestra Señora de la Asunción; a subsidiary chapel at El Caulote (Santa Ana) also served the municipio.
- **Key historical events:** The Mexican Revolution (1910–1920) disrupted civil registration compliance throughout Michoacán during much of the target period. This aligns with the documented gaps in Parácuaro's civil nacimientos for 1913–1915 and 1918.

## Boundary changes
- Parácuaro municipality has been stable since its 1861 formation. No boundary changes affecting the target period were returned by the place tools.
- The Diocese of Apatzingán, which currently holds the parish archive, was created in 1961 from the Diocese of Zamora. In 1905–1920, the Tierra Caliente including Parácuaro was under the Diocese of Zamora. The physical records are now archived at the Archivo Diocesano de Apatzingán (per FamilySearch Catalog, koha:162793), but a separate catalog note also references the Archivo Diocesano de Zamora — both archives may hold copies.

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)
- **Start date:** Municipio-level civil registration began 28 July 1859 (national law); vigorously enforced from 1867 (per [Mexico Civil Registration](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Mexico_Civil_Registration)). For Parácuaro, the FamilySearch Catalog shows nacimientos filmed from 1881.
- **What exists — nacimientos (births):** Continuous volumes are available and 100% name-indexed online for 1900–1912 and 1916–1922. A documented gap exists: no civil nacimientos volumes for 1913, 1914, 1915, or 1918 appear in FamilySearch volume_search or the catalog. The catalog film note for film 1096290 explicitly states only "Nacimientos 1910-1912, 1916-1917, 1919-1922" — those four years are absent. For Mauro Cruz Corona born ~1910, the 1910 nacimientos volume (DGS M98X-BWN, 53 images, 100% indexed) is directly relevant.
- **Specific target volumes (nacimientos, all 100% indexed, not full-text searchable):**
  - 1910: DGS 004871475_001_M98X-BWN
  - 1911: DGS 004871475_002_M98X-BWJ
  - 1912: DGS 004871475_003_M98X-BWV
  - 1916: DGS 004871475_004_M98X-BWK
  - 1917: DGS 004871475_005_M98X-BPZ
- **Where held:** Originals at Archivo del Registro Civil del Estado de Michoacán (per catalog notes). Online via FamilySearch collection [Mexico, Michoacán, Civil Registration, 1859-1940](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1916243); also at Ancestry (Michoacan, Mexico, Civil Registration Births, 1859-1934, https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/60415/).
- **What a nacimiento record contains:** Date and time of birth; child's name and gender; parents' names, ages, birthplaces, residence, marital status; paternal and maternal grandparents' names; number of previous children (sometimes).
- **Gaps:** 1913–1915 and 1918 are absent from the filmed/digitized civil nacimientos — likely a combination of Revolutionary-era non-compliance and lost volumes.

### Church records (Catholic bautismos)
- **Parish:** Nuestra Señora de la Asunción, Parácuaro — the main parish serving the municipio seat. A subsidiary chapel, Santa Ana, El Caulote (formerly Furicato), also recorded its own bautismos.
- **Archive:** Archivo Diocesano de Apatzingán (creator per FamilySearch Catalog koha:162793); catalog notes also reference Archivo Diocesano de Zamora.
- **Record types:** Bautismos, confirmaciones, matrimonios, información matrimonial, entierros. Separate registers were maintained for most.
- **Bautismos coverage and access for target period (all online, FamilySearch collection 1883388):**
  - 1890–1906: DGS 004087255_002 — 98% indexed, full-text searchable
  - 1906–1913: DGS 004737524_001_M9ZR-WQ1 — 96% indexed, full-text searchable
  - 1913–1917: DGS 004737524_002_M9ZR-W7M — 97% indexed, full-text searchable
  - 1918–1921: DGS 004737525 — 97% indexed, full-text searchable
- **El Caulote chapel (Santa Ana):** Bautismos 1902–1918 (DGS 4768334, indexed) and 1918–1936 (DGS 4768335, indexed), online via FamilySearch collection 1883388.
- **What a bautismo record contains:** Date and place of baptism; child's name, gender, and birth date; legitimacy; parents' names; godparents' names; before 1820, also social class and race.
- **Language:** Spanish throughout the target period.
- **Key point:** The Catholic bautismos fill the 1913–1915 and 1918 gaps in the civil record. A child born in those years would appear only in the parish register, not in any surviving civil nacimiento. Even for years when both exist, both should be searched — they are independent records with different information.

### Census records
- **1930 National Census:** The only digitized national census available for this period covers 1930. Mauro Cruz Corona would be approximately 20 years old in 1930. The municipio of Parácuaro is included. FamilySearch: [Mexico Census, 1930](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1307314) (catalog DGS 4107250, indexed, online). Also at Ancestry.
- **Earlier enumerations:** No earlier census available online for this municipio. No state-level census results were returned for Michoacán in this period.
- **Access:** The 1930 census is indexed and free at FamilySearch.

### Probate and court records
- **Types:** Wills, intestate administrations, guardianships, inventories. Held at the municipio courthouse or state archive.
- **Date range:** The FamilySearch Catalog returned no probate records for Parácuaro — this is a cataloguing gap rather than evidence the records do not exist.
- **Where held:** Likely at the Archivo Judicial or municipal courts in Parácuaro; originals not confirmed as digitized. No online access found.

### Land records
- **Survey system:** Mexico uses metes and bounds.
- **Land-distribution jurisdiction:** The FamilySearch wiki page for Mexico Land and Property was not fetched in this survey; colonial and early post-Independence land grants in Michoacán were administered by the state and federal governments. Nueva Italia was a large colonization enterprise — land concession records may be held at the Archivo General de la Nación (AGN) in Mexico City (http://www.agn.gob.mx/).
- **Where held:** AGN for federal concessions; state archive (Archivo General e Histórico del Poder Ejecutivo de Michoacán, Morelia) for state-level transactions. No online access for Parácuaro land records was identified.

### Military records
- **Relevant conflicts:** The Mexican Revolution (1910–1920) is the primary conflict for this period.
- **Record types:** Military service records, pension records, draft registrations.
- **Where held:** Archivo de la Secretaría de la Defensa Nacional (SEDENA), Mexico City (https://www.gob.mx/sedena/acciones-y-programas/expedicion-de-documentos). Limited online access; most require direct contact.

### Cemetery records
- **Online coverage:** FindAGrave and BillionGraves both have some coverage for Michoacán; searching the [Find a Grave Index for Michoacán cemeteries](https://www.findagrave.com/cemetery/search?cemetery-name=&cemetery-loc=Michoac%C3%A1n+de+Ocampo%2C+Mexico) is the best starting point.
- **Physical records:** Sexton records for the Parácuaro municipal cemetery are not confirmed as digitized.

### Newspaper records
- **Local papers:** No local newspaper identified for Parácuaro in the 1905–1920 period by the tools. State-level papers from Morelia may carry relevant legal notices.
- **Online access:** [Hemeroteca Nacional Digital de México](http://www.hndm.unam.mx/) has some historical Mexican newspapers.

### Immigration and emigration records
- **Border crossing records:** If the family moved between Guerrero and Michoacán (evidenced by sibling birth locations), no border crossing record exists for that internal movement. For potential migration to the United States, Ancestry holds [Border Crossings from Mexico to US, 1895–1964](https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/1082) and FamilySearch holds [US Border Crossings from Mexico to US, 1903–1957](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1803932).
- **Naturalizations:** Not applicable for domestic research in this period.

### Tax records
- **Types:** Property tax (predial), personal property.
- **Where held:** Municipal and state archives. Not confirmed as digitized for Parácuaro.
- **Substitute value:** Tax lists can substitute for missing census years and establish residence and property ownership.

### Other record types
- **Confirmaciones:** Catholic confirmation registers for Parácuaro, 1900–1923, exist online (DGS 004737531_002_M9ZR-4M5, full-text searchable; 0% name-indexed — must be browsed). A confirmation record records the confirmed person's name and godparent, which can help identify a child of unknown parentage as a sibling.
- **Información matrimonial (marriage investigation documents):** Extensive coverage 1898–1925, all 100% indexed online. These pre-marriage documents name the groom, bride, both sets of parents, and witnesses — excellent for identifying parents of anyone who married in or near Parácuaro.

---

## Repository guide

### Online repositories

| Repository | Collections for this place | Access |
|---|---|---|
| FamilySearch | Mexico, Michoacán, Civil Registration, 1859–1940 (collection 1916243) — nacimientos, matrimonios, defunciones, all indexed | Free |
| FamilySearch | Mexico, Michoacán, Catholic Church Records, 1555–1996 (collection 1883388) — bautismos, matrimonios, confirmaciones, información matrimonial, indexed | Free |

# Locality Guide: Nueva Italia (Parácuaro Municipality), Michoacán, Mexico (1905–1920)

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Formed:** Parácuaro municipality recognized 1861. Nueva Italia (Colonia Nueva Italia) is a community within this municipality and has no separate civil or ecclesiastical record-keeping jurisdiction.
- **Administrative center:** Parácuaro (the municipio seat), Michoacán
- **Parent jurisdiction:** State of Michoacán (became a Mexican state 22 December 1823); civil records held at the municipio level
- **Population during period:** No population data was returned by FamilySearch tools for this municipio. Nueva Italia is in the Tierra Caliente (hot lowlands) region of Michoacán.
- **Economy:** Agriculture, including large hacienda and colonization enterprises (Nueva Italia was itself a colonization project in the Tierra Caliente).
- **Religious denominations:** Roman Catholic, overwhelmingly dominant. The Parácuaro parish church is Nuestra Señora de la Asunción; a subsidiary chapel at El Caulote (Santa Ana) also served the municipio.
- **Key historical events:** The Mexican Revolution (1910–1920) disrupted civil registration compliance throughout Michoacán, directly explaining the documented gaps in Parácuaro's civil nacimientos for 1913–1915 and 1918.

## Boundary changes
- Parácuaro municipality has been stable since its 1861 formation. No boundary changes affecting the target period were returned by the place tools.
- The Diocese of Apatzingán, which currently holds the parish archive, was created in 1961 from the Diocese of Zamora. In 1905–1920, Parácuaro was under the Diocese of Zamora. The physical records are now at Archivo Diocesano de Apatzingán (per FamilySearch Catalog, koha:162793), but the catalog notes also reference Archivo Diocesano de Zamora — both archives may hold copies.

## Available record types

### Vital records (civil registration)
- **Start date:** Municipio-level civil registration began 28 July 1859 (national law); vigorously enforced from 1867 (per [Mexico Civil Registration](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Mexico_Civil_Registration)). Parácuaro filmed nacimientos start at 1881.
- **What exists — nacimientos (births):** Continuous volumes, 100% name-indexed, online for 1900–1912 and 1916–1922 (within the target period). A documented gap: no civil nacimientos volumes for 1913, 1914, 1915, or 1918 appear in either FamilySearch volume_search or the Catalog. The Catalog film note for DGS 4871475 explicitly lists only "Nacimientos 1910-1912, 1916-1917, 1919-1922."
- **Key target volumes (all 100% indexed, online via collection 1916243):**
  - 1910: DGS 004871475_001_M98X-BWN (53 images) — most relevant for Mauro born ~1910
  - 1911: DGS 004871475_002_M98X-BWJ (61 images)
  - 1912: DGS 004871475_003_M98X-BWV (70 images)
  - 1916: DGS 004871475_004_M98X-BWK (72 images)
  - 1917: DGS 004871475_005_M98X-BPZ (47 images)
- **What a nacimiento record contains:** Date and time of birth; child's name and gender; parents' names, ages, birthplaces, residence, marital status; paternal and maternal grandparents' names.
- **Where held:** Originals at Archivo del Registro Civil del Estado de Michoacán. Online at FamilySearch collection [Mexico, Michoacán, Civil Registration, 1859-1940](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1916243) and Ancestry [Michoacan, Mexico, Civil Registration Births, 1859-1934](https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/60415/).

### Church records
- **Parish:** Nuestra Señora de la Asunción, Parácuaro — the main parish. Subsidiary chapel Santa Ana, El Caulote (formerly Furicato), recorded its own bautismos.
- **Archive:** Archivo Diocesano de Apatzingán (catalog creator); catalog notes also reference Archivo Diocesano de Zamora.
- **Bautismos coverage for target period (all online, FamilySearch collection 1883388):**
  - 1890–1906: DGS 004087255_002 — 98% indexed, full-text searchable
  - 1906–1913: DGS 004737524_001_M9ZR-WQ1 — 96% indexed, full-text searchable
  - 1913–1917: DGS 004737524_002_M9ZR-W7M — 97% indexed, full-text searchable
  - 1918–1921: DGS 004737525 — 97% indexed, full-text searchable
- **El Caulote / Santa Ana chapel:** Bautismos 1902–1918 (DGS 4768334, indexed) and 1918–1936 (DGS 4768335, indexed), via collection 1883388.
- **What a bautismo record contains:** Date and place of baptism; child's name, gender, and birth date; legitimacy; parents' names; godparents' names.
- **Language:** Spanish. Records in this period are handwritten in formatted ledger registers.
- **Key point:** The Catholic bautismos fill the 1913–1915 and 1918 gaps in civil registration. Both record types should be searched even when both exist, as they contain different information.

### Census records
- **1930 National Census:** The only digitized national census available; covers Parácuaro municipio. FamilySearch: [Mexico Census, 1930](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1307314) (DGS 4107250, indexed, online). Also at Ancestry.
- **Earlier enumerations:** No earlier census found for this municipio in the tools.

### Probate and court records
- No probate records for Parácuaro were returned by the FamilySearch Catalog — a cataloguing gap, not necessarily evidence of absence. Originals likely at the municipio courthouse or state archive in Morelia.

### Land records
- Nueva Italia was a large colonization enterprise; land concession records may be at the AGN in Mexico City (http://www.agn.gob.mx/). No Parácuaro land records identified as digitized.

### Military records
- Mexican Revolution service records held at SEDENA (https://www.gob.mx/sedena). Limited online access; written request required.

### Cemetery records
- [FindAGrave index for Michoacán](https://www.findagrave.com/cemetery/search?cemetery-name=&cemetery-loc=Michoac%C3%A1n+de+Ocampo%2C+Mexico) and BillionGraves. Sexton records for Parácuaro not confirmed as digitized.

### Newspaper records
- No local newspaper identified for Parácuaro in 1905–1920. [Hemeroteca Nacional Digital de México](http://www.hndm.unam.mx/) has some historical state papers.

### Immigration/emigration records
- Border crossings Mexico to US: Ancestry collection https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/1082 (1895–1964); FamilySearch collection 1803932 (1903–1957).
- Internal migration between Guerrero and Michoacán is not recorded in border records; search civil registers of both states.

### Tax records
- Property and personal property tax records held at municipal and state archives. Not identified as digitized for Parácuaro.

### Other record types
- **Confirmaciones:** Parácuaro, 1900–1923 (DGS M9ZR-4M5, 0% name-indexed, full-text searchable — must be browsed). Useful for identifying siblings.
- **Información matrimonial (pre-marriage investigations):** 1898–1925, all 100% name-indexed online. Name both sets of parents and witnesses — excellent for identifying parents of anyone who married in Parácuaro.

---

| Ancestry | Mexico, Select Baptisms, 1560–1950 (https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/9297/) | Subscription |
| MyHeritage | Mexico Baptisms, 1560–1950 (https://www.myheritage.com/research/collection-30039/mexico-baptisms-1560-1950) | Subscription |

**Coverage of this survey:** 100 digitized volumes match Parácuaro, Michoacán in the 1900–1925 window (summary complete: true). All are online; no physical-only volumes among those surveyed.

### Physical repositories
| Repository | Holdings | Access method |
|---|---|---|
| Archivo del Registro Civil del Estado de Michoacán, Morelia | Original civil registers for Parácuaro | In-person or written request |
| Archivo Diocesano de Apatzingán | Original parish registers, Parácuaro and El Caulote | In-person or written request |
| Archivo Diocesano de Zamora | May hold additional copies of parish registers (per catalog note) | In-person or written request |
| AGN, Mexico City (http://www.agn.gob.mx/) | Land concessions, military, colonial records | In-person; some online |

---

## Records NOT online
- Civil nacimientos for 1913, 1914, 1915, and 1918 — no volumes exist at FamilySearch; Catholic bautismos (which ARE online) are the only available substitute.
- Probate and court records for Parácuaro.
- Land and tax records for Parácuaro.
- SEDENA military service records.
- Sexton / cemetery records.

---

## Known record losses
No tool result in this survey explicitly states that any Parácuaro record set was destroyed. The gap in civil nacimientos for 1913–1915 and 1918 is consistent with Revolutionary-era disruption of registration compliance, but the catalog and volume_search do not state those records were destroyed — they may exist in physical form at the state civil registry. The Catholic bautismos appear intact through this entire period.

---

## Research tips
1. **Search civil nacimiento 1910 (DGS M98X-BWN) and parish bautismo 1906–1913 (DGS M9ZR-WQ1) simultaneously** at FamilySearch — both are indexed and free. Per [Mexico Research Tips and Strategies](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Mexico_Research_Tips_and_Strategies): always search siblings' birth records to confirm and extend parentage findings.
2. **Search información matrimonial records (1898–1925, 100% indexed)** for a marriage of Mauro's parents before 1910. These pre-marriage investigation documents name the groom, bride, both sets of parents, and witnesses — a direct path to grandparental names.
3. **Search El Caulote (Santa Ana chapel) bautismos** (DGS 4768334, 1902–1918, indexed) if the main Parácuaro parish search yields nothing. Parish served different parts of the municipio.
4. **Search Guerrero civil records (FamilySearch collection 1918291)** in parallel. The sibling stubs place the family in Guerrero during 1913–1918 — exactly the years absent from Parácuaro civil nacimientos.
5. **Search the 1930 census.** Mauro Cruz Corona (~age 20 in 1930) should appear in the Parácuaro enumeration; household entry may name parents' birthplaces and ages.
6. **Account for name variants and transcription errors.** Per [Mexico, Michoacán, Catholic Church Records how-to](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Mexico,_Michoac%C3%A1n,_Catholic_Church_Records_-_FamilySearch_Historical_Records): abbreviations and alternate spellings are common. Browse nearby images after any index search.

entry.rationale: The Michoacán statewide civil birth register (collection 1916243) is name-searchable and 100% indexed for 1910 per the locality guide (loc_001). Per Mexico_Naming_Customs wiki, Mauro's compound surname Cruz Corona identifies his father's first surname as Cruz and his mother's first surname as Corona — search on Cruz (paternal) with Corona (maternal). A civil birth acta names both parents directly. The locality guide confirms the documented civil-register gap covers only 1913-1915 and 1918, so 1910 records are fully available.

The Parácuaro Catholic baptismal register (collection 1883388) is name-searchable and 96% indexed with full-text search, covering 1906-1921 per the locality guide (loc_001). Baptisms were recorded in parallel with civil registration and name the child's parents and godparents. This is the primary parallel source alongside item pli_001, and it covers the 1913-1915 civil gap years. Search Cruz (paternal) and Corona (maternal) per Mexico naming customs.

The locality guide (loc_001) identifies a second chapel — Santa Ana, El Caulote (formerly Furicato) — serving part of Parácuaro municipality, with bautismos 1902-1918 indexed on FamilySearch. If Mauro's family resided in the El Caulote area rather than the main parish center, his baptism would appear here rather than in collection 1883388 (item pli_002). Search here if item pli_002 yields nothing.

Three siblings recorded in the tree were born in Guerrero during the exact years Parácuaro's civil register has documented gaps: Miguel Cruz (24 Apr 1913, El Coco, La Unión, Guerrero), Liborio Cruz (23 Jul 1916, Pochutla, Coahuayutla, Guerrero), and Facundo Cruz (27 Nov 1918, Rosario, Coahuayutla, Guerrero). The Guerrero civil registration collection (collection 1918291) is name-searchable. Each sibling's birth acta would name the same father (surname Cruz) and mother (surname Corona) as Mauro's record, directly establishing both parents' full names. Search Cruz and Corona in La Unión and Coahuayutla municipalities for each sibling's name.

If the siblings' civil birth records in collection 1918291 (item pli_004) are absent for La Unión and Coahuayutla, the Guerrero Catholic church records (collection 1823323) are name-searchable and may hold the siblings' baptismal entries for the same period. Catholic baptisms name both parents. The collection covers 1576-1979 and includes parishes in both La Unión and Coahuayutla municipalities.

BCG standards require a dedicated search for the candidate parents' marriage. The father's surname is Cruz and the mother's is Corona (established by Mauro's compound surname per Mexico naming customs). They married before Mauro's birth circa 1910, most likely 1895-1910; the date window is bounded by the plausible marriage age of the parents. A civil marriage acta names both parties' parents (Mauro's grandparents), confirms the couple as a unit, and supplies the mother's full given name and her own maternal surname. Michoacán civil marriage volumes for Parácuaro are available on FamilySearch via the statewide civil registration collection (collection 1916243).

Mauro Cruz Corona died 21 April 1999 in Nueva Italia (Parácuaro municipality), Michoacán per the tree. Mexican civil death actas (defunciones) routinely name the deceased's parents by full name. This record carries secondary information (from whoever reported the death), but independently may confirm or supply parent names when birth and sibling records are absent or inconclusive. The date range is sized to the death year, not the birth window; files can testify to birth-era events. Search via the Michoacán statewide civil registration collection.

Per the Mexico_Military_Records wiki, Cartillas del Servicio Militar Nacional were issued to all males entering military service at age 18 and list the conscript's full name, date and place of birth, parents, and civil status. Mauro born ~1910 would have registered ~1928 at the Parácuaro ayuntamiento. These records are NOT on FamilySearch; they are held in the local ayuntamiento or at the Dirección General de Archivo e Historia, Miguel de Cervantes Zaavedra s/n, Col. Irrigación, 11640 México D.F. (SEDENA). Searching this record requires a written request to SEDENA or the Parácuaro ayuntamiento and is best attempted after FamilySearch sources above are exhausted.

guardrail_shadow_violations.detail: person_evidence link written for new tree person(s) I3 with no prior same_person call: a brand-new identity should be scored before it is asserted (person-evidence/SKILL.md doctrine; issue #963). Score them with the project-relative form, which assembles both documents for you: `same_person({ projectPath, assertionId, treePersonId: "I3" })`. `assertionId` is the assertion the link cites. The tool resolves the record itself and builds the tree side as that person's matching mob, so you hand-build nothing (person-evidence, 'Call it with references, not documents'). If this call was denied, the entire batch was rejected — including any ops in other sections — and must be re-issued after the same_person call. A relationship or marriage assertion names two parties and gets a link for each. The call is about the assertion's own `record_role` party by default; for the OTHER party add `recordRole` (or `recordPersonaId`) naming it. Reusing the first party's persona for the second is how a near-zero score gets manufactured and then explained away. If the tool answers that the record holds no persona for that party, or that the candidate is a stub minted from the very persona you would be scoring (circular), say so in the link's `rationale` and proceed — the gap is still recorded; the rationale is the record of why, not a waiver. How the assertion was RETRIEVED is not such a case: a full-text hit, an image, a PDF and a sidecar-less search are all scorable, because the tool derives the record side from the record's own assertions when it cannot fetch a document. A locally-minted tree id is NOT such a case: it scores on document content and must be scored.
